newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief deplores killing of Israeli schoolgirls.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief deplores killing of Israeli schoolgirls.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan deplored the killing on Thursday of seven Israeli schoolgirls by a Jordanian soldier on the border between the two countries and said the tragic incident highlighted the need to renew confidence in the Middle East peace process.

"The secretary-general was shocked by the news that a Jordanian soldier fired upon a group of Israeli schoolgirls, killing seven and wounding several others," a statement issued through his spokesman said.
"The secretary-general deplores this act of violence and extends condolences to the families of the victims and the government and people of Israel.

"Today's tragic incident highlights the need to renew confidence in the peace process whose objective is the achievement of a comprehensive, just and lasting settlement in the Middle East," the statement added.
The incident occurred at a time when the peace process is at a low ebb as a result of a number of recent developments.

These include a widely criticised Israeli decision to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in largely Arab East Jerusalem; an exchange of recriminations between Jordan's King Hussein and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu; and Palestinian dissastisfaction with Israel's decision to withdraw from 9 percent of occupied territory in the first of three scheduled pullbacks, instead of the 30 percent they said they had expected.

The General Assembly was expected to adopt a resolution by a large majority later in the day calling on Israel to rescind its decision to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a tree-lined hill between East Jerusalem and Bethlehem called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians.
